questions.q: In "Know your customer and market Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Count the market in units: how many subscribers could one area buy in a month? Use two public sources and your own count, then take the lower figure.
Keep an incident and near-miss log. Near-misses are free lessons.
Make a 12-month cash plan. Cash timing matters as much as profit: customers may pay late, suppliers may want money first.
Learn the tax regime that fits your size and write down which taxes you will collect and pay, and when.

questions.q: In "Rules, registration and data duties in Brazil Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Personal data of customers falls under Brazil's data protection law (LGPD). Collect only what you need, say why, keep it safe, and name who answers questions.
Set one measurable target for 90 days, such as 'raise repeat customers from 20% to 30%'.
Write a simple one-page terms sheet: what is included, what is extra, how to cancel.
Add one proof for each promise: a sample, a test result, a guarantee or a customer record.

questions.q: In "Design the offer Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Hold a ten-minute team check each day: yesterday's problem, today's plan, one risk.
Write a one-page standard procedure per stage: who, what, tool, time, record.
Describe the core offer in three lines: what is delivered (a network or connectivity service), the standard it meets, and the time it takes.
For the top five, choose a control: remove the hazard, replace it, guard it, train people, or use protective gear, in that order of preference.

questions.q: In "Run the work step by step Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write a one-page standard procedure per stage: who, what, tool, time, record.
Create two options at most, so choice stays easy.
In telecom: Protect tower and cabinet work with fall protection, electrical isolation and radio-frequency exposure limits.
In telecom: Monitor revenue per user, churn, and cost per site; churn above 3% a month needs a fix.

questions.q: In "Safety, quality and risk Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Train by showing, doing with support, then doing alone with a check. Record sign-off per task.
Find the sector rules for telecom: licences, inspections, professional registers. List each with the office that issues it and the renewal date.
Check that insurance and legal duties match the risk you actually carry.
Choose three measures: speed, quality (errors per 100) and customer rating. Review them every week.

questions.q: In "People, skills and service Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Plan the renewal of licences, equipment and skills a year ahead.
Ask each customer how they found you, and record it. Spend more where the record shows results.
Write a role card for each person: purpose, five tasks, the standard for each, and who to ask for help.
In telecom: Offer a plan with real measured speeds, a clear price and no hidden charges.

questions.q: In "Money: cost, price and break-even Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: For the top five, choose a control: remove the hazard, replace it, guard it, train people, or use protective gear, in that order of preference.
Fix the cause of a defect, not the symptom. Ask 'why' five times and record the answer.
Make a 12-month cash plan. Cash timing matters as much as profit: customers may pay late, suppliers may want money first.
Keep an incident and near-miss log. Near-misses are free lessons.
